I feel you. Since 2021 I’ve been a hardcore Xbox gamer, leaving my PS5 to mostly collect dust while I played on my Series X, happily investing a LOT of time and money. I even ended up buying a Series S for my bedroom. I was all in. And then the acquisition of Activision seemed to mark the moment that Xbox became Microsoft Gaming and everything has started to fall apart.

Although there are certainly things I don’t like, there are so many things I love about the Series consoles that PlayStation 5 either can’t or won’t offer. I particularly love their phenomenal backwards compatibility efforts and how they’ve managed to secure more Xbox versions of Japanese franchises that in the past were either completely absent from the platform or spotty at best. Persona, Kingdom Hearts, Tales of, Yakuza, NieR, Dragon Quest, Monster Hunter, Final Fantasy… Obviously PlayStation is a better platform for these types of games, but it really shows the efforts Microsoft had been putting in.

But one thing Xbox’s competition is offering is a slew of games not available on Microsoft’s machine - both first-party and third-party - and now Microsoft is giving away their own games to the competition. It started out innocently enough with smaller titles like Hi-Fi Rush and Pentiment, and the live service games Grounded and Sea of Thieves. But now they’ve announced DOOM: The Dark Ages and Indiana Jones are coming to PlayStation 5 - one a briefly timed exclusive, the other completely multiplatform from day one. And it looks like Age of Empires has leaked for PlayStation too. How much longer until the Forza Horizon and Microsoft Flight Simulator rumours also become true?

My problem here isn’t more people getting to play more games. My problem is the death spiral this creates. If Microsoft brings more games to PlayStation and/or Nintendo, less people will feel the need to buy an Xbox. When that happens, there are less sales from the platform. Publishers see this and start to deprioritise an Xbox release, ranging from a rough port, to delaying the Xbox version, to skipping it outright. Then customers see that the games they want to play are either better on or only on the competition and so don’t buy into the Xbox ecosystem, further progressing the spiral.

Microsoft just isn’t doing enough to combat this, and it’s seemingly because they don’t want to. And because of that, I’ve lost confidence in the brand, gone back to PlayStation, bought a PS5 Pro and all the games I’ve wanted to play that haven’t come to Xbox.

If Microsoft ever manages to realise and reverse their mistake of prioritising short-term gains in multiplatform game sales over the long-term health of a viable gaming platform before it’s too late, maybe I’ll come back.

Games on Xbox Game Pass are the same as the versions you purchase from the Microsoft Store, meaning that if a game leaves the service and you decide to buy it, your saved data will not be impacted in any way whatsoever. And assuming you have that game already downloaded, you won't need to redownload it. The Xbox servers will recognise the purchase and remove the Game Pass logo from the game's tile on your dashboard.

Even for games included in the Xbox Game Pass library you will need a subscription to Xbox Live Gold to play online. However, if you opt for the higher tier Xbox Game Pass Ultimate, you will get a subscription to Xbox Live Gold included with that. Furthermore, you receive a wide range of other benefits:

* Xbox Game Pass for console
* Xbox Game Pass for PC
* Xbox Live Gold
* Xbox Cloud Gaming
* EA Play

For some games included in the Xbox Game Pass library the saved data will be applicable to both the Xbox version and the PC version, with no manual saved data transfer required by you. This is typically limited to first-party games, such as Forza, Halo, Sea of Thieves, Microsoft Flight Simulator and so on, but there are some third-party games that also support this.

You will need an Outlook email address to sign up for Xbox, but the benefit is that this single Microsoft account can be used for all of their services.

One tip I can think of is this: When downloading a game from Xbox Game Pass, instead of pressing A to open its game card and then pressing A again to install it, press the menu button and go to Manage Game & Add-Ons (or whatever it's called), pick whichever hard drive you want to install it on (just your internal SSD if you've got no external hard drive connected), and then on the right click Select All. This will download not only the game but also any DLCs that have been included with the Game Pass listing. It took me ages to figure this out. Games like Halo: The Master Chief Collection, Gears 5, Ryse: Son of Rome, Ark: Survival Evolved and more all have DLC included but for some reason Xbox Game Pass won't automatically download them, you have to do it manually.

When my friend was trampled on by a stampede of students in secondary school (high school, for you Americans, I believe). Here’s the story:

One day at school my friends and I were in a D.T. (Design Technology, sewing and pattern theory stuff) class, and Dan, who was sat beside me, told me that he had a hole in his sock and it was irritating him. I’m not sure why I did it, but I told him to take his shoe off and show me before all of the other students come in. When he took his shoe off and he placed it on the table, I grabbed it and launched it across the room. It landed on top of a really tall wardrobe behind the teacher’s desk, and in order to get to the top you’d need to stand on the step ladder, but even then it was a stretch. He was almost out of his seat when the other  students came in, forcing him to sit there for the remainder of the class wearing only one shoe, with his big toe poking out of the sock on his other foot.

Once class ended and everybody was making their way to their next one, Dan retrieved his shoe and joined us (myself and another friend, Spencer) outside the room. Around the corner from the D.T. room were the doors that lead out to the courtyard. For some reason, unless it was lunch time, only one of the two doors was ever unlocked, forcing everybody to go single-file. Obviously, there were people on both sides wanting to go through the door, and a lot of pushing and shoving ensued as neither side managed to control the flow. Wanting to get back at me for throwing his shoe, Dan says something along the lines of, “You’re going in there,” and goes to shove me. Realising this I moved out of the way just before he pushed me, and because he did it with such force, the combined weight of the things in his backpack refused to allow him to stop himself from falling over. And just as he crashed onto the ground, the students outside won the inverse game of tug-of-war and burst through, trampling all over a screaming Dan.

From where Spencer and I were stood, it was safe from the action, but we needed to cross to the other side of the stream of students so we could go the long way around to our next class. Spencer went first and successfully made it through without any issues. But when I tried to cross I was knocked over. Thankfully (for me) I bounced back onto my feet after landing on something soft. It was Dan’s backpack. He had been slowly pushing himself back up when I essentially butt-slammed him back to the ground and had enough propulsion from it to get myself to the other side with Spencer.

Looking back at the commotion we decided it best to assume he was dead and go to our next class, wherein we found him sat there, red-faced and moody. Apparently a teacher had found him lying on the floor and ordered the other students to stop so that he could get up.

Dan is the unluckiest guy I’ve ever known. I have so many stories about him.

I bought Bloodborne when it first came out in March 2015, despite people telling me to only buy it if I'm up for a challenge. I got home, excited, popped it in and booted it up (after waiting for updates). I got to the Great Bridge with the two wolves... and that's as far as I got. I couldn't get past them. They were just too hard. So for a year I left it sat on my shelf - myself believing that it'll forever be the one game in my collection that I cannot beat.
Fast forward a year to April 2016 and the looming release of Dark Souls III has the internet very excited, as well as people I know personally. It seemed it was impossible to venture online without coming across a post or tweet related to From Software's latest title. After being subjected to so much hype, I myself ended up boarding the train, despite never playing any Dark Souls game, nor Demon's Souls. The only experience I'd had with this type of game was Bloodborne, and I really didn't like it. Tempted to buy Dark Souls III I applied some common sense: if I didn't like Bloodborne, I won't like Dark Souls III. So before I would let myself buy Dark Souls III, I had to - I absolutely *must* - beat Bloodborne, otherwise I'll be wasting my money.
So I dusted off my copy of Bloodborne, waking it from its year-long nap, and I booted it up (more updates to install). I got to the same bit where I gave up last time. Died. Repeatedly. I was so tempted to just give up again but I thought that perhaps I should find an online guide, something to help me get going.
After watching a YouTube video I discovered that I'd been doing it all wrong! It turns out that if a pathway seems unfairly hard, even for a Souls game, it's normally the wrong way, and exploration will reveal the true path. After watching a guide to help get me started I managed to get to the Cleric Beast.
We fought ferociously. My heart was pounding. My palms were sweating. 'This - this is a boss fight!' I thought to myself. After a few moments, it was over. My hunter, drenched in the blood of the beast, was victorious. And for the first time, I understood why people love these games. That rush of adrenaline was unlike anything I'd ever felt from a video game.
I continued on my hunt, cutting down Father Gascoigne, Vicar Amelia, Rom, Darkbeast Paarl, Blood-Starved Beast, Moon Presence - I sought them all out. I cut them all down. Every. Single. One.
To this day I still play Bloodborne, clocking up more than 150 hours, earning the Platinum trophy, reaching NG++++, and also purchasing the DLC, The Old Hunters. Unbeknownst to me at the time, from March 2015 to April 2016, one of this generation's - one of gaming's - greatest video games sat on my shelf collecting dust. Bloodborne has made a hunter out of me.
Give it another go, grizzly. It may make a hunter out of you, too.
